meta.title: District drought — OAE SPEI ดัชนีภัยแล้ง รายอำเภอ (obj #1)
meta.label: MODELLED — OAE-published SPEI per amphoe (ERA5-Land reanalysis). An official model product: not station rainfall, not a disaster declaration. Snapshot 2026-06 only; 5 districts carry a suspect 0.0 (grid gap) and are unclassified.
meta.source: MODELLED index, not a raw meteorological observation and not a disaster declaration. SPEI (Standardized Precipitation-Evapotranspiration Index) computed by OAE from ERA5-Land Daily Aggregated reanalysis climate data (ECMWF Climate Reanalysis, served via Google Earth Engine Data Catalog) — i.e. MODELLED/derived from measured global reanalysis precipitation + temperature, aggregated to a monthly mean per amphoe (Thai district). This IS the exact 'OAE SPEI by district' product the user named: OAE is the publisher of record on data.go.th, and the metric is genuinely SPEI, genuinely at amphoe resolution, genuinely dated. It is NOT: (a) a Thai ground-station-only product (the underlying grid is a global reanalysis, downscaled/aggregated to district polygons — so treat as MODELLED, same provenance tier as the pipeline's existing HDX rainfall proxy, one step more official since OAE is the compiling government agency), (b) a DDPM drought-disaster declaration (no administrative/legal weight), (c) a multi-month per-district history (see gaps below).

headline: 338 of 928 districts sit at moderate-or-worse drought on OAE's SPEI (2026-06): 2 extreme, 110 severe, 226 moderate. Driest: เขาคิชฌกูฏ (จันทบุรี), มะขาม (จันทบุรี), เมืองจันทบุรี (จันทบุรี), ท่าใหม่ (จันทบุรี), เขาสมิง (ตราด).
